exporter_layout_dialect_run.note: Fresh repeat of the same 235-test command to retain complete output; no source edits.

epilogue_formula_review.verdict: Equivalent for all current shared-tile coordinates
epilogue_formula_review.proof: For column<64, row*64 and column have disjoint bits; (linear & (7<<6))>>3 equals (row&7)<<3 and occupies only column bits, so XOR can be performed on column before row addition.

interpretation_limits: Static instruction counts are not dynamic execution counts or latency.
Address/integer proxy includes loop/control arithmetic and excludes some moves/predicate instructions; compare full opcode counts too.
No performance benefit is inferred from one-round timings.
inherited_probe_audit.kernel_diff: Only shared_offset helper expression/comment changed; column<64 allows separating row*64 and column xor row swizzle.

independent_review.performance_conclusion: No timing benefit inferred from static counts or exploratory one-round timings; final repeated measurements handled separately.

retained_changes: Layout-proven i32 matrix offsets with i64 fallback and final pointer arithmetic.
Verified carry-free lane/window address factoring, otherwise the general offset path.
Cooperative-copy thread remainder by verified positive thread count: an identity for all legal callers, exposing bounds without changing partial-atom zero filling.
Causal-only infinity repair matches unchanged CuTeDSL.
Factored output swizzle uses disjoint row/column bits; exhaustive equality across all 4,096 shared tile coordinates.
limitations: Static and runtime cases remain distinct.
Rust has a 1D launch grid versus the reference 3D grid with identical CTA count.
Profiles explain concrete code-generation differences, not an exact latency decomposition.
Reference LDGSTS includes LTC128B; Rust does not.
Runtime noncausal retains a localized matrix-load wait and other scheduling/address differences.
